title: APA SOLAR REGULATOR MODULE FOR BATTERY BUSES - EXPRO PLUS
description: The Advanced Power Architecture (APA) is a standard concept for the Power Conditioning and Distribution Unit (PCDU). APA follows the interoperable and interchangeable modularity approach applied for the project ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) that started in 2020. APA is aimed to be fully compatible with ADHA so that together they will form the kern of a satellite platform.As ADHA, APA is composed of two elements: a standardized Unit rack (element 1) that providesstandard services to a set of Power Modules (element 2) that populates the rack to make an APA PCDU. The power unit can be built upon modules from different manufacturers, based on performances, cost, programmatic constraints. This approach allows strong reduction of development time and recurrent costs, faster development and adoption of more performing technologies in great part enabled by the envisaged interoperable and interchangeable modules that compose the system.The definition the Advanced Power Architecture and related Standardization of the development ofthe APA element 1 (rack product) is being addressed in a dedicated activity funded by the Preparation Element of the DPTD and by the Future EO Program (ESA/IPC(2022)1,add.42). The modules that compose the element 2 of the APA are subject to several TDE activities. Element 1 outputs (APA Unit requirements and standard requirements for APA Modules) will be used as inputs to Element 2 activities. Element 2 outputs (APA Modules) will then be used as input to Element 1 (for the validation of standard power modules requirements and overall APA architecture).GaN advantages (e.g. high switching frequency, thermal performance, inherently radiation tolerant),allowing a more compact power cell, will be fully exploited in combination with resonant power conversion techniques. Digital control techniques provides flexible and reliable control of the power cell and a first level failure detection isolation and recovery (FDIR)in the module.This activity aims to develop the Solar Regulator module (SAR) for battery buses with Maximum Power Point Tracking capabilities.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Consolidation of APA Requirements (generic and specific modules)- Trade off and evaluation of the most promising Conversion Power Cell topologies- Preliminary and detailed design definition- Manufacturing and testing the module- Contribution to the APA Unit integration and test, including APA standardised documentationand interoperability/interchangeability test.

title: TGO-MEX RADIO OCCULTATION - EXPRO+
description: RO occurs when the transmitter of a radio signal appears to set behind a planet, as viewed from a receiving station. The radio signal is refracted by the atmosphere and ionosphere causing a frequency shift; analysing this frequency shift allows reconstruction of a high-resolution vertical profile of density (and thus pressure and temperature) in the neutral atmosphere and ionospheric electronabundances in the ionosphere. Spacecraft-to-Earth RO has been carried out for many decades by planetary missions, but the opportunities for this are limited by the orbital geometry and ground station availability.

title: ACTIVE LOCAL STRUCTURAL CONTROL OF VERY LARGE SPACE STRUCTURES - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of this activity is to develop a breadboard of a local active control system, which demonstrates the capability of locally regulating the stiffness of very large structures in space.Description: Large space structures are expected to exhibit structural modes at low frequency likely to couple with the AOCS control system. For very large structures it is expected that the attitude control will be achieved by distributed sensors and actuators, which may potentially result in relative high loads and displacements. Past activities have shown the potential of local structural control by using strain sensors co-located with active elements for local structural stiffening (e.g. based on piezo technology).This activity is expected to provide an assessment on the critical aspects of very large structures, including: Interaction between structure and AOCS (criticality of structure stiffness vs. mass). Feasibility to reduce structural resonance through passive and/or active structuraldamping. Criticality of pointing and stability requirements, e.g. for solar power generation maintaining sun-point for solar generator surface and Earth pointing for power transmission. ROM evaluation of internal loading on structure to ensure satisfactory capability of structural design, material selection and joining technologies. Feasibility for redundancy in the design and performance of very large structures, assuming potential failure in structure or structural joining elements as well as on AOCS sensors and actuators over the anticipated in-orbit lifetime.In consideration of the above, this activity targets the development of a local active control system breadboard together with an on-ground testbed representative of very large structures in space to demonstrate this technology.The activity will encompass thefollowing tasks: Identify candidate sensing and stiffness regulators suitable for local strain sensingand stiffening. Assess and optimise the integration of strain sensing and stiffness regulators into structural elements in view of optimising the local controllability of stiffness. Design a distributed control system that drives the local stiffening systems toachieve global stabilisation and control goals. Define a suitable verification and validation process for the designed distributedcontrol system. Define and setup a ground testbed representative of very large structures in space. Demonstrate the distributed control system on a suitable scaled breadboard,adapted for laboratory environment and deployed on the ground testbed.NOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: END-TO-END MODELLING OF THE RADIATION HARDNESS ASSURANCE PROCESS - EXPRO+
description: Objectives: To develop an integrated software toolkit to assess the relative contributions to overall errors and uncertainties in the radiation hardness assurance process and estimate the true risk of failures. Description: The current process for Radiation Hardness Assurance (RHA) attempts to ensure compliance to mission robustness, reliability and availability with respect to radiation. This includes a range of measures addressed at different stages of the process. environment models are often applied with confidence levels and margins which in isolation may not sufficiently mitigate risk, the transport of radiation through shielding can incorporatea great deal of hidden margin (depending on the level of detail of the radiation model) but this can also be reduced to near-zero through detailed analysis and effects in components based on test data are highly susceptible to component specifics combined with other degradation parameters and temperature variations. Given this myriad of factors the true risk of component failure is not easy to discern. This activity shall address Radiation Hardness Assurance (RHA) as an integrated approach from radiation environment modelling to component acceptance to determine true risk levels for the end-to-end process. This shall include assessment of the probabilities of component failure for various environments using different methods for capturing environmental variability, radiation model fidelity and uncertainties in component test data and related statistical approaches. This shall be able to incorporate a digital representation of the spacecraft for radiation transport, test data for components and a range of orbital environments thereby spanning multiple disciplines in spacecraft design and quality assurance and extracting benefits from adopting a Model-Based System Engineering (MBSE) approach. The system shall incorporate estimates of errors and uncertainties at each step of the process to derivean estimate of the true risk of failure. This activity shall encompass the following tasks: - Investigate the requirements and definition of process by consultation with radiation experts in industry as well as at ESA - Establish the use cases and collect relevant radiation effects data to test in the software; - Design of the software architecture leveraging existing assets to link orbits, environments, propagation and effects; - Develop algorithms to propagate uncertainties through the different steps of the RHA process;- Derivation of "true risk" estimates and comparison with current approaches; - Make recommendations for the maturation of this integrated (MBSE) approach Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community Licence.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required.
